normalization: Originals as fetched under original/, pinned to a commit of the repository named in origin.items. text/<slug>.txt is the TEI reduced to plain text by seat.py (rebuild/corpora/ea-corpora-27), notes and apparatus dropped, divisions kept. No text was corrected by hand.
scope: Six commentators of the school of Ammonius and its neighbours, seven texts: the commentaries on the Categories by Ammonius, Simplicius, Philoponus, Olympiodorus and Elias, Olympiodorus's Prolegomena, and David's Prolegomena to philosophy. Each prolegomenon sets the reader's questions before a treatise; one of them is whether the book is genuine, and several give the ways books came to be spurious: the ambition of royal collectors, the goodwill of pupils who wrote under the teacher's name, and homonymy of authors, of works or of commentaries. Elias names Ptolemy's catalogue of a thousand works with the life and the will. Elias's and David's commentaries on the Isagoge, and the Prolegomena of the anonymous and of Simplicius's other prefaces, are not seated.
verified_loci: Olympiodorus, Prolegomena: the question of the genuine — 'πρῶτον μὲν διὰ πόσους τρόπους ἐνοθεύοντο τὰ βιβλία καὶ ποῖά εἰσιν κριτήρια τὰ δυνάμενα διαχωρίζειν τὰ γνήσια ἀπὸ τῶν νόθων' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Olympiodorus, Prolegomena: three ways books were made spurious, the kings' ambition, the pupils' goodwill, homonymy — 'ἢ διὰ φιλοτιμίαν τῶν βασιλέων ἢ δι’ εὔνοιαν τῶν μαθητῶν ἢ διὰ ὁμωνυμίαν' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Ammonius, In Cat.: the fifth head, whether the book is spurious or genuine — 'πέμπτον εἰ νόθον ἢ γνήσιον τοῦ φιλοσόφου τὸ βιβλίον' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Ammonius, In Cat.: many composed works and inscribed them with Aristotle's name — 'πολλοὶ γὰρ αὑτῶν συντιθέντες ἐπέγραφον τῷ Ἀριστοτέλους ὀνόματι' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)
Simplicius, In Cat.: the heads to be set out before a treatise of Aristotle — 'εἰ γνήσιον τοῦ φιλοσόφου τὸ βιβλίον'

Philoponus, In Cat.: three occasions for the spuriousness of Aristotle's writings, the first homonymy of authors — 'τρεῖς γὰρ αφορμαὶ γεγόνασι τοὐ νοθεύεσθαι τὰ συγγράμματά του Ἀριστοτέλους' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Philoponus, In Cat.: Andronicus of Rhodes on beginning with logic — 'ὁ δὲ τούτου διδάσκαλος Ἀνδρόνικος ὁ Ῥόδιος ἀκριβέστερον ἐξετάζων' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Elias, In Cat.: Ptolemy's catalogue, a thousand works, with the life and the will — 'χιλίων τὸν ἀριθμόν, ὥς φησι Πτολεμαῖος ὁ Φιλάδελφος ἀναγραφὴν αὐτῶν ποιησάμενος καὶ τὸν βίον αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν διάθεσιν' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Elias, In Cat.: royal ambition, Iobates collecting Pythagoras and Ptolemy collecting Aristotle — 'ἢ διὰ φιλοτιμίαν βασιλικήν· Ἰοβάτους γὰρ τοῦ Λιβύων βασιλέως συναγαγόντος τὰ Πυθαγόρου καὶ Πτολεμαίου τὰ Ἀριστοτέλους' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Elias, In Cat.: books aged artificially for the market — 'τινὲς καπηλείας χάριν τὰ τυχόντα συγγράμματα λαμβάνοντες' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)

Elias, In Cat.: works inscribed to the teachers, Socratics under Socrates and Pythagoreans under Pythagoras — 'ὡς τὰ Πυθαγόρου καὶ Σωκράτους ἐπιγραφόμενα βιβλία μὴ ὄντα Σωκράτους ἢ Πυθαγόρου ἀλλὰ Σωκρατικῶν καὶ Πυθαγορικῶν' (the TEI mixes composed and decomposed Greek; the locus is given in the text's own characters)
why_seated: The prolegomena are where the tradition wrote its rules for keeping one author per name. The study reads them for what the test of genuineness presupposes, and for the mechanisms of spuriousness they name, one of which, the pupils' goodwill, describes the many writing under one.
